title: Flowcharts as testable execution models
goal: Follow a flowchart’s arrows and check the free-delivery boundary.

prerequisites.text: You understand if/else branching and comparisons.

sections.title: From the task to an operation
paragraphs: Delivery is free for an order total of at least 1000. A smaller nonnegative total has a fee of 150. A negative total is invalid. Follow the arrows: start → test total<0 → on “no”, test total>=1000 → one result → end.

A diamond is a question with labelled yes/no exits. A rectangle is an action such as output. >= includes equality; else if asks the next question only after the previous answer was no. The example’s number is in the source; stdin is empty.

sections.title: Follow a flowchart’s arrows and check the free-delivery boundary.
trace: The order is valid; continue to the next question.
Equality is included, selecting free delivery.
The other branches do not run.

sections.title: Change one condition and check the prediction
paragraphs: Check total=999, then total=-1; name the questions visited.
For -1, the first question answers yes; the second is never needed.

sections.title: When the result differs
paragraphs: Replacing >= with > incorrectly charges an order of exactly 1000. Test the boundary itself.

sections.title: Now solve your own task
paragraphs: Set a passing score of 60, with valid scores 0..100. Output invalid, pass or retry. Check -1,59,60,101.
Practice contains a separate starter. Predict the result before changing your program. Returning to the example does not replace your source.

selfcheck.prompt: What output follows the specified change? Check total=999, then total=-1; name the questions visited.
selfcheck.feedback: For 999, both questions answer no. For -1, the first question answers yes; the second is never needed.

selfcheck.prompt: Set a passing score of 60, with valid scores 0..100. Output invalid, pass or retry. Check -1,59,60,101.
selfcheck.feedback: Compare the output with the readable reference case below. Explain each change using the objects or operations in this topic. For -1, 59, 60, 101 the answers are invalid, retry, pass, invalid. Using > 60 instead of >= 60 incorrectly gives retry at the boundary score 60.

practice.title: Independent variation
practice.task: Set a passing score of 60, with valid scores 0..100. Output invalid, pass or retry. Check -1,59,60,101.
criteria: Compare the output with the readable reference case below.
Explain each change using the objects or operations in this topic.
For -1, 59, 60, 101 the answers are invalid, retry, pass, invalid. Using > 60 instead of >= 60 incorrectly gives retry at the boundary score 60.
practice.hint: For 999, both questions answer no. For -1, the first question answers yes; the second is never needed.

steps.action: Set a passing score of 60, with valid scores 0..100. Output invalid, pass or retry. Check -1,59,60,101.
Write your solution in a separate starter; keep your previous work.
Compare actual output with your prediction and explain any difference.
